senses.d: chosen in preference to another

ex.t: I was selected for the journey, and at ten o'clock we started, in a light, high-wheeled gig, which ran so easily that after the four-wheeled cab it seemed like nothing.
ex.zh: 这趟活挑了我去；十点我们动身，拉的是一辆轻巧的高轮单马车，跑起来轻快得很，比起四轮马车简直像没拉东西。

ex.t: His limbs were in proportion, and I had selected his features as beautiful.
ex.zh: 它的四肢是匀称的，我也曾挑出它那些相貌，叫它们好看。

ex.t: I fear that he will become an idler unless we yield the point and permit him to enter on the profession which he has selected.
ex.zh: 我怕他会变成一个闲荡的人，除非我们让这一步，准许他入他选定的那一行。

senses.d: pick out, select, or choose from a number of alternatives
x: Take any one of these cards
Choose a good husband for your daughter

ex.t: Now, mustering the spare poles from below, and selecting one of hickory, with the bark still investing it, Ahab fitted the end to the socket of the iron.
ex.zh: 接着，他把备用的木杆从下面集拢来，挑了一根山核桃木的，上面还带着树皮，把杆端装进铁叉的套筒里。

ex.t: But before I am run away with by my feelings on this subject, perhaps it will be advisable for me to state my reasons for marrying--and, moreover, for coming into Hertfordshire with the design of selecting a wife, as I certainly did.”
ex.zh: 不过在我为这件事让感情冲得走开之前，也许还是先把我要结婚的理由说一说为好——还要说说我为什么到赫特福德郡来，而且确实是抱着择妻的打算来的。”

ex.t: Then, selecting a little side gallery, I made my essay.
ex.zh: 然后我挑了一条小小的侧廊，做起试验来。

senses.d: the act of choosing or selecting
x: your choice of colors was unfortunate
you can take your pick

senses.d: an assortment of things from which a choice can be made
x: the store carried a large selection of shoes

senses.d: the person or thing chosen or selected
x: he was my pick for mayor

senses.d: a natural process resulting in the evolution of organisms best adapted to the environment
a passage selected from a larger work
x: he presented excerpts from William James' philosophical writings

ex.t: But we shall always call the best selection of such tales "Grimm's Tales": simply because it is the best collection.
“Then, I think,” said Mr. Lorry, “that I was very unhandsomely dealt with, and that I ought to have had a voice in the selection of my pattern.
ex.zh: “那么我想，”洛里先生说，“待我可真不厚道，挑我这个样子的时候，本该让我也说句话。

ex.t: Now, a judicious selection from these with the least possible delay, and the burying of them, or otherwise getting of them out of harm’s way, is within the power (without loss of precious time) of scarcely any one but myself, if any one.
ex.zh: 那么，尽可能快地把这些文件挑拣一批，埋起来，或者用别的法子弄到安全地方——又不损失宝贵时间——这几乎除了我，谁也没有这个本事，就算有人有，也难说。

senses.d: the act of choosing or selecting
x: your choice of colors was unfortunate
you can take your pick

senses.d: an assortment of things from which a choice can be made
x: the store carried a large selection of shoes

senses.d: the person or thing chosen or selected
x: he was my pick for mayor

senses.d: a natural process resulting in the evolution of organisms best adapted to the environment
a passage selected from a larger work
x: he presented excerpts from William James' philosophical writings

ex.t: The lion took it with care and caution, made his selections from it, and his remarks upon it, and the jackal assisted both.
ex.zh: 狮子小心谨慎地接过，从中挑挑拣拣，又对它发表议论，豺狗则两头都帮着。

ex.t: The professional elocutionist, Mrs. Evans, came and chatted with her, telling her that she had a charming voice and “interpreted” her selections beautifully.
ex.zh: 那位职业朗诵家埃文斯太太也过来跟她聊，说她嗓子好听，选的篇子“演绎”得美。

ex.t: Pray give me the results of your newspaper selections.”
ex.zh: 请把你从报上选出的结果告诉我。”

senses.d: tending to select; characterized by careful choice- John Mason Brown
x: an exceptionally quick and selective reader

senses.d: characterized by very careful or fastidious selection
x: the school was very selective in its admissions

ex.t: We improve our favourite plants and animals—and how few they are—gradually by selective breeding; now a new and better peach, now a seedless grape, now a sweeter and larger flower, now a more convenient breed of cattle.
ex.zh: 我们靠选择育种，慢慢改良偏爱的动植物——而它们是那么少；忽而是一种更好的新桃，忽而是无籽葡萄，忽而是一种更香更大的花，忽而是一种更合用的牛。

senses.d: pick out, select, or choose from a number of alternatives
x: Take any one of these cards
Choose a good husband for your daughter

senses.d: of superior grade
x: choice wines
prime beef

senses.d: selected or chosen for special qualifications
x: the blue-ribbon event of the season

ex.t: If a personality fascinates me, whatever mode of expression that personality selects is absolutely delightful to me.
ex.zh: 一个性格若叫我着迷，它无论选哪种表达方式，对我都绝对可喜。

senses.d: your consciousness of your own identity
a person considered as a unique individual
x: one's own self

senses.d: (used as a combining form) relating to--of or by or to or from or for--the self
x: self-knowledge
self-proclaimed

ex.t: They have forgotten the highest of all duties, the duty that one owes to one's self.
And thus when Liza entered, holding Nana, the nursery seemed quite its old self, very dark, and you would have sworn you heard its three wicked inmates breathing angelically as they slept.

I feel exquisite pleasure in dwelling on the recollections of childhood, before misfortune had tainted my mind and changed its bright visions of extensive usefulness into gloomy and narrow reflections upon self.

senses.d: voluntary self-punishment in order to atone for some wrongdoing

ex.t: He is supposed to live in a continuous frenzy of hatred of foreign enemies and internal traitors, triumph over victories, and self-abasement before the power and wisdom of the Party.
ex.zh: 他应当生活在持续的狂热里：仇恨外敌和内奸，为胜利而欢腾，在党的力量和智慧面前自贬。

ex.t: In our world there will be no emotions except fear, rage, triumph, and self-abasement.
ex.zh: 在我们这个世界里，除了恐惧、暴怒、胜利和自我贬低，不会有别的情绪。

senses.d: used especially of behavior

ex.t: He shook in a self-abnegating way, as one who shook for Tellson and Co.
ex.zh: 他握得克己自制，像一个替特尔森公司握手的人。

senses.d: renunciation of your own interests in favor of the interests of others

ex.t: It was easy to promise self-abnegation when self was wrapped up in another, and heart and soul were purified by a sweet example.
ex.zh: 当自己整个儿裹在另一个人身上，心与魂又被一个甜美的榜样洗过的时候，许下克己的愿是容易的。

senses.d: designated or chosen by yourself
x: a self-appointed guardian of public morals

ex.t: Regularly, each morning after he had finished his breakfast, she performed her self-appointed task, till he came to look for her ministrations as much as he did for Thornton’s.
ex.zh: 每天早上他吃完早饭，她就干她给自己派的这活，从不间断；后来他盼她的照料，跟盼桑顿的一样。

senses.d: the trait of resolutely controlling your own behavior

ex.t: I was aware also that I should often lose all self-command, all capacity of hiding the harrowing sensations that would possess me during the progress of my unearthly occupation.
ex.zh: 我也知道自己会常常完全失去自制，失掉一切遮掩的能力——遮掩在我那非人的工作进行中占住我的那些撕裂心肺的感觉。

ex.t: “You began the evening well, Charlotte,” said Mrs. Bennet, with civil self-command, to Miss Lucas.
ex.zh: “你晚上开了个好头，夏洛特，”班纳特太太客客气气、按捺着自己对卢卡斯小姐说。

senses.d: aware of yourself as an individual or of your own being and actions and thoughts- D.M.Potter
x: self-conscious awareness
self-conscious about their roles as guardians of the social values

senses.d: excessively and uncomfortably conscious of your appearance or behavior
x: self-conscious teenagers
wondered if she could ever be untidy without feeling self-conscious about it

ex.t: And Lord Henry struck a light on a dainty silver case and began to smoke a cigarette with a self-conscious and satisfied air, as if he had summed up the world in a phrase.
The pulse and passion of youth were in him, but he was becoming self-conscious.
ex.zh: 青春的脉搏与激情在他身上，可他正变得自我意识。

senses.d: in an uncomfortably self-conscious manner
x: the little girl self-consciously recited the poem

ex.t: Self-consciously, with his authoritative arms breaking the way, we pushed through the still gathering crowd, passing a hurried doctor, case in hand, who had been sent for in wild hope half an hour ago.
ex.zh: 我们不自然地，由他那副权威的手臂开路，挤过仍在聚拢的人群，经过一个匆匆赶来的医生，手里提着箱子——半个钟头前有人抱着狂热的希望去请的。

senses.d: constituting a complete and independent unit in and of itself
x: the university is like a self-contained city with shops and all amenities

senses.d: in full control of your faculties
x: the witness remained collected throughout the cross-examination
perfectly poised and sure of himself

ex.t: Hard and sharp as flint, from which no steel had ever struck out generous fire; secret, and self-contained, and solitary as an oyster.
ex.zh: 他像燧石一样又硬又利，从没有哪块钢能从他身上打出一点慷慨的火星；他又像牡蛎一样缄默、自闭、孤零零。

ex.t: “Mr. Barry, what has happened to her?” she gasped, more white and shaken than the self-contained, sensible Marilla had been for many years.
ex.zh: “巴里先生，她怎么了？”她喘着问，脸色比平时白得多，也比这个镇定明白的玛丽拉多少年来都更慌。

ex.t: For in that case each would still be a self-contained universe, freed for ever from the sobering influence of external danger.
ex.zh: 因为那样一来，每一个仍然是一个自足的宇宙，永远摆脱外部危险那种使人清醒的影响。

senses.d: the act of denying yourself; controlling your impulses
the trait of resolutely controlling your own behavior

ex.t: “I suppose you’re homesick--some people have so little self-control in that respect.
ex.zh: “我猜你想家了——有些人在这一层上真没一点自制。

ex.t: Although the oldest, Jo had the least self-control, and had hard times trying to curb the fiery spirit which was continually getting her into trouble.
ex.zh: 乔在家里虽算大的，却最管不住自己；那股火性总给她惹麻烦，她想压住它，可吃了不少苦头。

ex.t: “You will excuse my calling so late,” she began, and then, suddenly losing her self-control, she ran forward, threw her arms about my wife’s neck, and sobbed upon her shoulder.
ex.zh: “请原谅我这么晚来打扰，”她开口道，可随即控制不住自己，抢上前去，双臂搂住我妻子的脖子，伏在她肩上哭起来。

senses.d: a misconception that is favorable to the person who holds it

ex.t: Whatever gloss the various spectators put upon the interest, according to their several arts and powers of self-deceit, the interest was, at the root of it, Ogreish.
ex.zh: 不管各类看客凭各自的本事和自欺的本领，给这份兴趣涂上什么光彩，这兴趣归根到底还是吃人的。

senses.d: a misconception that is favorable to the person who holds it

ex.t: Nor is the history of fanatics half so striking in respect to the measureless self-deception of the fanatic himself, as his measureless power of deceiving and bedevilling so many others.
ex.zh: 而在狂信者的历史里，比起他自己那种无边的自欺来，他那种无边的、迷惑并蛊惑许多别人的本领还要惊人得多。

ex.t: In the dream his deepest feeling was always one of self-deception, because he did in fact know what was behind the wall of darkness.
ex.zh: 在梦里，他最深的感受总是一种自欺，因为他其实知道那堵黑墙后面是什么。

ex.t: He remembered remembering contrary things, but those were false memories, products of self-deception.
ex.zh: 他记得自己记得相反的东西，可那些是假记忆，是自欺的产物。

senses.d: the trait of practicing self discipline
the act of denying yourself; controlling your impulses
renunciation of your own interests in favor of the interests of others

ex.t: The mutilation of the savage has its tragic survival in the self-denial that mars our lives.

Waste forces within him, and a desert all around, this man stood still on his way across a silent terrace, and saw for a moment, lying in the wilderness before him, a mirage of honourable ambition, self-denial, and perseverance.
ex.zh: 内心是荒废的力气，四周是一片荒漠；这人在穿过一片寂静平台的路上站住，有一瞬看见前面的荒野里躺着海市蜃楼——光荣的抱负、克己和坚忍。

ex.t: “It would be ungenerous to affect not to know that your self-denial is to be referred to your consideration for her father.
ex.zh: “要是假装不知道你的克制是出于对她父亲的体谅，那就不厚道了。

senses.d: willing to deprive yourself
used especially of behavior

ex.t: They have such an eatable look that the most self-denying stranger can hardly keep his hands off.
ex.zh: 它们看上去那样可吃，最克己的陌生人见了也几乎忍不住要伸手。

senses.d: the act of killing yourself
x: it is a crime to commit suicide

senses.d: the act of destroying yourself
x: his insistence was pure self-destruction

ex.t: It needs an act of self-destruction, an effort of the will.

senses.d: the trait of practicing self discipline
the act of denying yourself; controlling your impulses

ex.t: It's merely a question of self-discipline, reality-control.
ex.zh: 这只是一个自律的问题，控制现实的问题。

ex.t: You are here because you have failed in humility, in self-discipline.
ex.zh: “你到这里来，是因为你在谦卑和自律上失败了。”

senses.d: educated by your own efforts rather than by formal instruction

ex.t: But it is a still greater evil to me that I am self-educated: for the first fourteen years of my life I ran wild on a common and read nothing but our Uncle Thomas' books of voyages.
But it is a still greater evil to me that I am self-educated: for the first fourteen years of my life I ran wild on a common and read nothing but our Uncle Thomas’ books of voyages.
ex.zh: 但对我更大的不幸，是我全靠自学：我生命最初的十四年，是在荒地上野跑过来的，除了托马斯叔叔那些航海书，什么也没读。

senses.d: evident without proof or argument
x: an axiomatic truth
we hold these truths to be self-evident

ex.t: You also believe that the nature of reality is self-evident.
ex.zh: “你还相信现实的本质是不言自明的。”

ex.t: But this statement, which to an orthodox ear merely conveyed a self-evident absurdity, could not have been sustained by reasoned argument, because the necessary words were not available.
ex.zh: 但这句话在一个正统的耳朵听来只传达出一种自明的荒谬，无法用论证来支撑，因为所需的词并不存在。

ex.t: To take the first example to hand, I very clearly perceive that in your bedroom the window is upon the right-hand side, and yet I question whether Mr. Lestrade would have noted even so self-evident a thing as that.”
ex.zh: 就拿手边第一个例子说：我看得很清楚，你卧室的窗子是在右手边；可我怀疑莱斯特雷德先生连这么一目了然的事也未必注意到。”

senses.d: the act of helping or improving yourself without relying on anyone else

ex.t: Self-help is the best help.
ex.zh: 求人不如求己。

senses.d: hypnosis induced by yourself

ex.t: Partly it was a sort of hymn to the wisdom and majesty of Big Brother, but still more it was an act of self-hypnosis, a deliberate drowning of consciousness by means of rhythmic noise.
ex.zh: 一半是向老大哥的智慧与威严唱的赞歌，更多的却是一种自我催眠，有意用有节奏的噪声把意识淹没。

senses.d: an inflated feeling of pride in your superiority to others
an exaggerated opinion of your own importance

ex.t: The insipidity, and yet the noise--the nothingness, and yet the self-importance, of all these people!
There is a mixture of servility and self-importance in his letter which promises well.
ex.zh: 他这封信里有一种卑顺与自负的混合，这是好兆头。

senses.d: voluntarily assumed or endured
x: self-imposed exile

ex.t: To Elizabeth, however, he voluntarily acknowledged that the necessity of his absence had been self-imposed.
ex.zh: 不过对伊丽莎白，他自己承认：那不得不缺席的缘故，是他自己给自己定的。

senses.d: taking advantage of opportunities without regard for the consequences for others
concern for your own interests and welfare

ex.t: To be friendless is indeed to be unfortunate, but the hearts of men, when unprejudiced by any obvious self-interest, are full of brotherly love and charity.
ex.zh: 没有朋友确实是不幸，可人心若不被任何明显的私利所偏，是充满手足之爱和仁慈的。

senses.d: a feeling of sorrow (often self-indulgent) over your own sufferings

ex.t: Was it all self-pity, loneliness, or low spirits?
ex.zh: 这全是自怜、孤单，还是心气低落？

senses.d: in full control of your faculties
x: the witness remained collected throughout the cross-examination
perfectly poised and sure of himself

ex.t: He was otherwise quite self-possessed, bowed to the Judge, and stood quiet.
ex.zh: 除此以外，他十分镇定，向法官鞠了一躬，静静站着。

ex.t: How near to her heart the echoes of her child’s tread came, and those of her own dear father’s, always active and self-possessed, and those of her dear husband’s, need not be told.
ex.zh: 她孩子脚步的回声离她的心有多近，她自己亲爱的父亲那总是活跃而从容的脚步的回声有多近，她亲爱的丈夫脚步的回声有多近，都不必说了。

ex.t: They say that men who have seen the world, thereby become quite at ease in manner, quite self-possessed in company.
ex.zh: 人家说，见过世面的人，举止就十分从容，在众人面前也十分镇定。

senses.d: the trait of resolutely controlling your own behavior

ex.t: Devoutly thankful to Heaven for his recovered self-possession, he thought, “There is but another now,” and turned to walk again.
ex.zh: 他虔诚地感谢上天让他恢复了镇定，心想：“现在只剩一个钟头了，”就转身再走。

ex.t: Anne gave one gasping little scream which nobody ever heard; she was white to the lips, but she did not lose her self-possession.
ex.zh: 安妮低低惊呼了一声，谁也没听见；她嘴唇都白了，可她没有慌。

ex.t: Self-possession was fully restored to her, and in the reaction from that horrible moment of powerlessness she recited as she had never done before.
ex.zh: 她完全镇定了；从方才那可怕的一刻缓过来，她念得比从前任何时候都好。

senses.d: a feeling of deep regret (usually for some misdeed)
the act of blaming yourself

ex.t: In making me the offer, you must have satisfied the delicacy of your feelings with regard to my family, and may take possession of Longbourn estate whenever it falls, without any self-reproach.
ex.zh: 你向我求婚，总算是顾全了你对我家那份细致的心意；日后浪搏恩的产业什么时候落到你手里，你都可以坦然收下，不必自责。

ex.t: Fixed there by the keenest of all anguish, self-reproach, she could find no interval of ease or forgetfulness.
ex.zh: 最尖利的痛苦——自责——把它钉在那里，她找不到一刻轻松或忘怀。

ex.t: The self-reproach and contrition which are displayed in his remark appear to me to be the signs of a healthy mind rather than of a guilty one.”
ex.zh: 在我看来，他这话里流露的自责与悔恨，倒是一个健全心灵的表现，而不是有罪之心的表现。”

senses.d: a feeling of deep regret (usually for some misdeed)
the act of blaming yourself

ex.t: The monster continued to utter wild and incoherent self-reproaches.
ex.zh: 那怪物继续发出狂乱、不连贯的自责。

senses.d: the quality of being worthy of esteem or respect
x: it was beneath his dignity to cheat
showed his true dignity when under pressure

ex.t: It will restore my self-respect, for I was shedding tears freely before Ruby came along.
ex.zh: 这能恢复我的自尊，因为鲁比来之前我正大把掉眼泪。

ex.t: I’d rather see you poor men’s wives, if you were happy, beloved, contented, than queens on thrones, without self-respect and peace.”
ex.zh: 我宁可看着你们做穷人的妻子，只要你们快活、被人疼爱、心满意足；也不愿你们做宝座上的王后，却没有自尊，没有安宁。”

ex.t: “He has, however, retained some degree of self-respect,” he continued, disregarding my remonstrance.
ex.zh: “不过他还保留着几分自尊。”他不理会我的抗议，继续说。

senses.d: exhibiting restraint imposed on the self
x: an effective temperateness in debate

ex.t: His frank acceptance of the situation marks him as either an innocent man, or else as a man of considerable self-restraint and firmness.
ex.zh: 他坦然接受这个局面，说明他要么是个无辜的人，要么是个极能自制、极有定力的人。

ex.t: Hardship and freedom: conditions under which the active, strong, and subtle survive and the weaker go to the wall; conditions that put a premium upon the loyal alliance of capable men, upon self-restraint, patience, and decision.
ex.zh: 是艰苦与自由：在这样的条件下，活跃、强壮、机敏者得以生存，弱者被淘汰；这样的条件奖励能干者之间的忠诚结盟，奖励自制、耐心与决断。

senses.d: acting with less concern for yourself than for the success of the joint activity

ex.t: For a moment my soul was elevated from its debasing and miserable fears to contemplate the divine ideas of liberty and self-sacrifice of which these sights were the monuments and the remembrancers.
ex.zh: 有一刻，我的灵魂从它那些低贱而可怜的恐惧里被抬起来，去思索自由和自我牺牲的神圣观念——这些景物正是那些观念的纪念碑和提醒者。

ex.t: I believe that she is capable of heroic self-sacrifice and that anything dishonourable would be repugnant to her.”
ex.zh: 我相信她能做出英勇的自我牺牲，任何不光彩的事都会让她厌恶。”

ex.t: Don’t let us talk about it any more, and don’t try to persuade me that the first good action I have done for years, the first little bit of self-sacrifice I have ever known, is really a sort of sin.
ex.zh: 我们别再谈这个了，也别想说服我，说我多年来做的第一件善事、我所知道的第一次小小的自我牺牲，其实是一种罪。

senses.d: willing to deprive yourself
